claims.claim: Information Age reports that ASIC assessors found the AI output made strange choices about what to highlight.

claims.quote: made strange choices about what to highlight

claims.claim: Ninety-one percent of the AI responses in the BBC study were flagged as containing at least some issues.
claims.source: BBC, 'Representation of BBC News content in AI Assistants', February 2025
claims.quote: 91% of responses contained at least 'some issues'

claims.claim: The BBC study's ratings were made by 45 journalists reviewing 362 AI responses in their own areas of expertise.
claims.source: BBC, 'Representation of BBC News content in AI Assistants', February 2025

claims.claim: On a like-for-like BBC-to-BBC comparison the share of responses with significant issues of any type fell from 51 percent to 37 percent between the two rounds.
claims.source: BBC and European Broadcasting Union, 'News Integrity in AI Assistants', October 2025

claims.claim: The BBC-EBU authors conclude that AI assistants remain an unreliable way to access and consume news despite measured improvement.
claims.source: BBC and European Broadcasting Union, 'News Integrity in AI Assistants', October 2025
claims.quote: still not a reliable way to access and consume news

claims.claim: Hallucination rates on Supreme Court cases were highest for the oldest and the newest cases, a non-linear relationship with case age.
claims.source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, 'Large Legal Fictions', Journal of Legal Analysis (arXiv v2, 21 June 2024)
claims.quote: are most common among the Supreme Court's oldest and newest cases

claims.claim: Hallucinations were least common among the Supreme Court's post-war Warren Court cases of 1953 to 1969.
claims.source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, 'Large Legal Fictions', Journal of Legal Analysis (arXiv v2, 21 June 2024)
claims.quote: among its post-war Warren Court cases (1953-1969)

claims.claim: Dahl and colleagues report that the models performed better on cases that are newer and more salient, the opposite temporal direction to the HiST-LLM history result.
claims.source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, 'Large Legal Fictions', Journal of Legal Analysis (arXiv v2, 21 June 2024)
claims.quote: LLMs perform better on cases that are newer, more salient

claims.claim: The authors report that the models struggle to gauge their own level of certainty without post-hoc recalibration.
claims.source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, 'Large Legal Fictions', Journal of Legal Analysis (arXiv v2, 21 June 2024)
claims.quote: struggle to accurately gauge their own level of certainty

claims.claim: The authors warn that a model's peak performance may lag several years behind the current state of legal doctrine.
claims.source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, 'Large Legal Fictions', Journal of Legal Analysis (arXiv v2, 21 June 2024)
claims.quote: LLMs' peak performance may lag several years behind the current state

claims.claim: The SimpleQA authors report that models consistently overstate their stated confidence relative to their measured accuracy.
claims.source: Wei, Karina, Chung et al. (OpenAI), 'Measuring short-form factuality in large language models' (SimpleQA), arXiv, 7 November 2024

claims.claim: History is one of SimpleQA's tagged topics, with 173 of the benchmark's 4,326 questions.
claims.source: Wei, Karina, Chung et al. (OpenAI), 'Measuring short-form factuality in large language models' (SimpleQA), arXiv, 7 November 2024

claims.claim: LexisNexis marketed Lexis+ AI as delivering 100 percent hallucination-free linked legal citations.

claims.quote: Lexis+ AI delivers 100% hallucination-free linked legal citations
